ann_32.text: This part acts on 116 of 242 training patients (48%), and 77 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 58-year-old man with 1 vessel coloured, a flat ST segment, 1.6 mm of ST depression, signs of left ventricular hypertrophy and a reversible thallium defect), the predicted risk is above 99% with or without it, so it changes only slightly (on the training data only).

Through it, more ST depression on exercise (0 to 2.8 mm) raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 12% to about 32%, and it adds risk only once ST depression rises above about 1.2 mm: for the typical patient with this bend (a 56-year-old man with signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG), going from 0 to 3.5 mm moves it from about 14% to about 51% (on the training data only).
Through it, fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL and a reversible thallium defect each raise a typical patient's predicted risk from about 12% to about 18% (on the training data only).
More ST depression clearly raises the predicted risk more with a reversible thallium defect (from about 27% to about 76%, against about 12% to about 32% without it).

A downsloping ST segment raises it more if fasting blood sugar is 120 mg/dL or less (from about 12% to about 42%, against about 3% to about 10% above 120 mg/dL). The model has little data on this: only 17 training patients (a downsloping ST segment).

ann_33.text: This part acts on only 19 of 242 training patients (8%), women whose chest pain is brought on by exercise; 12 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 57-year-old woman with chest pain on exercise, a flat ST segment, 1.0 mm of ST depression and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG), it raises the predicted risk from about 9% to about 43% (the model has little data on this; on the training data only).
Through it, chest pain brought on by exercise and being a woman each raise that patient's predicted risk from about 9% to about 43% (on the training data only).
Across the whole model, being a woman lowers the predicted risk slightly more if exercise does not bring on chest pain (from about 12% to below 1%, against about 12% to about 2% with it).

ann_34.text: This part acts on 74 of 242 training patients (31%), and 13 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 51-year-old man with non-anginal chest pain, 0.2 mm of ST depression and a maximum heart rate of 169 beats per minute), it slightly lowers the predicted risk, from about 1% to below 1%.
Through it, non-anginal chest pain, a higher maximum heart rate and an abnormal thallium scan each change the predicted risk only slightly (on the training data only).
A higher maximum heart rate (118 to 175 beats per minute) clearly lowers the predicted risk more with non-anginal chest pain (from about 3% to below 1%, against about 22% to about 8% otherwise).

A thallium scan that is not normal raises it more if the chest pain is not non-anginal (from about 12% to about 37%, against about 1% to about 4% with non-anginal chest pain; on the training data only).

ann_35.text: For a typical patient, the model clearly gives a lower predicted risk of heart disease with typical angina (below 1%), non-anginal chest pain (about 1%) or atypical angina (about 7%) than with no chest pain symptoms (about 12%).

Going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 12% to about 98%, a flat ST segment raises it to about 76%, a reversible thallium defect to about 37%, more ST depression on exercise (0 to 2.8 mm) to about 32%, and higher cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL) from about 5% to about 31% (on the training data only).

Higher resting blood pressure (110 to 155 mm Hg) raises it from about 7% to about 22%, while a maximum heart rate of 175 rather than 118 beats per minute lowers it from about 22% to about 8%, being a woman to below 1%, and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 3% (on the training data only).

A thallium result coded 4 raises it to about 90% (2 patients) and a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers it to about 3% (15 patients); the model has little data on this, and both hold on the training data only.
Older age (42 to 66 years) and a resting ECG that is not normal raise it only slightly (on the training data only).

ann_32.original: Hypothesis: hidden gate 557 = ReLU(1.283*oldpeak + 0.559*thal:7 - 1.076*slope:3 - 0.417*fbs:0 + 0.085) is a one-sided ischaemia-evidence detector. It switches on mainly with exercise-induced ST depression (oldpeak), more readily when there is a reversible thal defect (thal:7), is pushed down by a downsloping ST segment (slope:3, which is clinically counter-intuitive; it is rare, 7%, and the direct linear core has no slope:3 term, so this is probably how the network absorbs slope:3 at all), and slightly by normal fasting sugar (fbs:0). It enters the logit with weight +0.746, so it only ever adds risk. Evidence (train, n=242): closed form exact (single ReLU); active on 47.9% of patients (83% with thal:7, 27% without); max 4.72, logit contribution SD 0.78; sensitivity oldpeak 0.62 > slope:3 0.52 > thal:7 0.27 > fbs:0 0.20; replacing it by its mean drops train AUC of the logit from 0.947 to 0.938, the largest of the three gates.
ann_32.proposed: A part that acts on about half the patients; through it, ST depression above about 1.2 mm raises the predicted risk, more so with a reversible thallium defect.

ann_33.original: Hypothesis: hidden gate 1239 = ReLU(0.571*sex:0 + 0.903*exang:1 - 0.853) is a Boolean AND of female sex (sex:0) and exercise-induced angina (exang:1). Evidence (train, n=242): truth table of the standardised one-hot inputs gives activation 1.199 for women with exang (n=19, positive rate 63%) and exactly 0 for the other three cells (male/no exang n=96 pos 40%; male/exang n=63 pos 76%; female/no exang n=64 pos 14%; the male+exang pre-activation is -0.004, just below the threshold). Weighted +1.730 into the logit it adds +2.07, which cancels most of the direct female protective term (-1.573*sex:0 contributes -2.18 for women vs +1.14 for men): the network learns that exercise angina erases the female advantage. Active on 7.9% of patients, logit contribution SD 0.56; mean-ablation drops train AUC 0.947 -> 0.940. Closed form exact.
ann_33.proposed: A part that acts only on 19 women whose chest pain is brought on by exercise and raises their predicted risk.

ann_34.original: Hypothesis: a protective high-exercise-capacity gate. Serial chain thal:3 -> 3818 -> 2124. 3818 = ReLU(1.003*thal:3 - 0.192) is a normal-thallium indicator taking only the values 0 (abnormal thal) and 0.702 (normal thal, 56% of patients). 2124 = ReLU(1.338*thalach + 0.763*cp:3 - 0.108*3818 - 0.932) fires when maximum heart rate is high, much more readily with non-anginal chest pain (cp:3): active on 80% of cp:3 patients but 10.5% of others (30.6% overall, max 2.88). It enters the logit with weight -0.918, so it only ever lowers risk, adding a hinge to the direct linear thalach (-0.470) and cp:3 (-0.743) terms. The thal:3 branch only moves the threshold by -0.076 (sensitivity 0.025 vs thalach 0.41, cp:3 0.23) and is nearly inert. Evidence (train, n=242): closed form exact; logit contribution SD 0.49; mean-ablation drops train AUC only 0.947 -> 0.945, the weakest of the three gates.
ann_34.proposed: A part that acts on about a third of patients, few of whom had heart disease; through it, a higher maximum heart rate lowers the predicted risk more with non-anginal chest pain.

ann_35.original: Root hypothesis: an additive composition that is essentially logistic regression plus three one-sided ReLU corrections. Logit z = -0.680 + LINEAR CORE + 0.746*st_depression_gate + 1.730*female_exang_and_gate - 0.918*thalach_cp3_protective_gate, and the prediction is sigmoid(z) (get_formula renders the output as ReLU, but for this binary task the model applies a sigmoid to the output pre-activation). LINEAR CORE = 19 direct input->output edges, dominated by ca (+2.607, number of vessels), sex:0 (-1.573, women lower risk), chol (+0.870), slope:1 (-0.833, upsloping ST protective), cp:1 (-0.785), slope:2 (+0.743), cp:3 (-0.743), fbs:0 (+0.627), trestbps (+0.519), thal:7 (+0.490), thalach (-0.470), sex:1 (+0.390), thal:4 (+0.383), thal:6 (-0.351), cp:4 (+0.312); age, restecg:0, exang:0/1 near zero. cp:2, fbs:1, restecg:1, restecg:2 are unused. Corrections: (a) ischaemia evidence (ST depression, reversible thal defect) adds risk; (b) women with exercise angina lose most of their sex protection (AND gate, +2.07 logit); (c) high max heart rate, especially with non-anginal pain, removes extra risk. Evidence (train, n=242): accuracy 0.876, AUC 0.947. Linear core logit SD 4.90 vs gates 0.78 / 0.56 / 0.49. Linear core alone AUC 0.930; mean-ablating each gate gives AUC 0.938 / 0.940 / 0.945, so together the nonlinear parts add ~+0.017 train AUC. SHAP (probability scale): ca 0.170 >> sex:0 0.080 > slope:1 0.063 > cp:3 0.058 > slope:2 0.053 > thal:7 0.050 > chol 0.038 > thalach 0.034 > oldpeak 0.029. Function preservation of the refactored model 1.8e-15; all leaf closed forms exact up to 3-s.f. display rounding (max 0.027).
ann_35.proposed: Typical angina, non-anginal chest pain and atypical angina lower the predicted risk compared with no chest pain symptoms. More vessels coloured, a flat ST segment, a reversible thallium defect, more ST depression, higher cholesterol and higher resting blood pressure raise it; a higher maximum heart rate, being a woman and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL lower it.

summary.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results, predicted risk about 12%), the model clearly gives a much lower predicted risk of heart disease with typical angina (below 1%), non-anginal chest pain (about 1%) or atypical angina (about 7%).

Going from 0 to 2 vessels coloured by fluoroscopy raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 12% to about 98%, and a flat rather than upsloping ST segment at peak exercise raises it to about 76% (on the training data only).

More ST depression on exercise raises the predicted risk, and even more so if the thallium scan shows a reversible defect: going from 0 to 2.8 mm clearly moves it from about 27% to about 76% with that defect, against about 12% to about 32% without it.
Being a woman lowers a typical patient's predicted risk from about 12% to below 1%, and higher cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL) raises it from about 5% to about 31% (on the training data only).

One small part acts only on 19 training patients, women whose chest pain is brought on by exercise, and raises their predicted risk from about 9% to about 43% (the model has little data on this; on the training data only).

parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: hidden gate 1239 = ReLU(0.571*sex:0 + 0.903*exang:1 - 0.853) is a Boolean AND of female sex (sex:0) and exercise-induced angina (exang:1).
